messages:
incident-bot: Paging: P95 latency >1200ms for /v1/generate in us-west-2 (hosted). Severity: Sev2. Pager: @erica. Customers impacted: multiple low-volume hosted tenants.

erica: Acknowledged. I'm on-call. Starting initial triage — grabbing traces, perf counters, node health.

mike: I'm nearby. Any recent infra changes? kernel or kube node updates?

erica: Rolling logs show a kernel upgrade window 02:03-02:07 UTC on a subset of the serving pool. Noted model variants also saw a spike at 02:04.

sam: Pulling p50/p95 metrics now. From our dashboards: p50 80ms -> 170ms around 02:04, p95 280ms -> 1270ms. Request rate steady.

jordan: Confirmed — QPS didn't increase. Heatmap attached in console (link: https://console.redwood.example/incident/4098765432).

nina: Perf counters snapshot (top summary):
```
# perf top - snapshot
cpu-clock: 67% user
irq/softirq: 18%
context-switches: up 3x
__sched__: increased syscall latency
```
Looks like syscall or scheduling stalls.

mike: dmesg excerpt from one affected node:
```
[Feb 14 02:03:21] kernel: kworker/1:2: soft lockup - CPU#1 stuck for 23s
[Feb 14 02:03:22] kernel: audit: type=1701 audit(...): auid=4294967295
```
Potential kernel regression.

erica: Good catch. Which kernel version rolled?

sam: Nodes moved from 5.15.0-48 -> 5.15.0-52 during maintenance window. Rollout targeted non-prod but affected some prod nodes due to label mismatch.

alex-prod: Customer impact note: 4 tenants reported elevated latency, 2 reported slow interactive responses. No increased error rate, just slowness. Logged CSAT tickets 1124, 1125.

mike: Mitigation options: 1) Rollback kernel on affected nodes, 2) Evacuate pods off affected nodes to non-upgraded nodes, 3) Route traffic to eu-west-1 fallback for new requests. Which do we prefer for quick mitigation?

erica: Step 1: Evacuate pods from the worst nodes (cordon + drain) to get them off 5.15.0-52. Step 2: temporary routing rule to avoid the us-west-2 subset during drain.

jordan: I'll apply an emergency routing policy: route policy id rw-emer-4098 -> exclude node pool us-west-2-kernel-52. Rolling now.

nina: While draining, capture perf and trace spans from a retained node. Run: sleuth record --targets=serve --duration=120s --out=/tmp/trace-4098.json

erica: Running sleuth now, collecting traces and dmesg. Also pulling kernel perf counters: "perf record -a -o /tmp/perf-4098.data -- sleep 60".

sam: After routing change, p95 dropped to ~350ms within 90s. p50 back to ~95ms. Looks like routing helped.

alex-prod: Notifying affected customers with templated update. Will mention mitigation and that we're investigating root cause.

mike: For RCA tracking: hypothesis A = kernel scheduling regression in 5.15.0-52 causing soft lockups; hypothesis B = interaction between our continuous batching and kernel change. We'll capture kernel perf and batching metrics.

erica: Assigning RCA lead: mike. Mike -> assemble timeline: node upgrade times, drain events, p50/p95 deltas, trace span examples, perf samples.

mike: Ack. I'll own timeline and gather artifacts. Plan: write timeline + attach traces to the incident doc, include perf flamegraphs, and correlate with deploy logs.

jordan: Final note: keep cluster scaling disabled until we confirm this isn't autoscaler related. Also preserve at least 2 affected nodes for deeper postmortem.

erica: Thanks everyone. Next steps: mike to publish RCA draft in #incidents-docs within 24h, nina to attach perf traces, sam to export timeseries panels. If anything changes I'll update here. :thumbsup:
